correctness.rationale: An all-n decomposition expresses X_n as the ordinary-intersecting complex with independent contractible four-set simplices attached along octahedral 2-spheres. Their integral fundamental cycles become oriented tetrahedral boundaries in the nerve model; Hurewicz upgrades homological boundary identification to homotopy attaching maps. The resulting third simplex skeleton has C(n-1,4) spheres. Its signed relative chains give Λ^4 of the integral sum-zero lattice. Independent finite face predicates, acyclic Morse matchings and characters corroborate n=6.

value.rationale: Canonical two-subset Kneser graphs and almost-intersecting families yield a uniform infinite-family homotopy classification and full integral homology symmetry module. The finite four-point containment is not itself the new result; the attaching-map and wedge/representation identifications supply motivated structural topology beyond isolated Betti numbers.
